prerequisites: Ability to apply multidisciplinary knowledge to problem-solving
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills for the application of materials engineering.
Know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Engineering.

Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Study of weldability in general. Welding metallurgy. Residual stresses.
Scientific and technological knowledge of welding processes and related techniques for materials most commonly used in Metal Construction.
Application of the most used inspection procedures for evaluating the quality of welded joints.
Ability to write and develop procedures for the welded fabrication of structures and other mechanical assemblies.
Facility in handling specifications and standards related to the construction and quality of welded joints.
Define processes and establish welding procedures, determining phases, operations, equipment, and tools, considering quality and economic criteria.

Scientific and technological knowledge about welding processes. Welding metallurgy. Weldability of different materials and application of the most used inspection procedures for evaluating the quality of welded joints and ensuring quality requirements.
Ability to write and develop procedures for the welded fabrication of structures, pressure vessels, and other industrial equipment.
Ability to handle specifications and standards related to the construction and quality of welded joints.

syllabus_topics: Weldability of C-Mn and micro-alloyed steels
Weldability of quenched and tempered steels
Weldability of C-Mo and Cr-Mo steels
Quality and Inspection of welded joints
Design and calculation of welded joints
assessment_rules: Attendance at 3 mandatory laboratory practice sessions is required; non-submission or unjustified absence results in automatic failure for both ordinary and extraordinary calls. For progressive evaluation, the final grade is calculated as 40% from two progressive tests, 10% from laboratory practices, and 50% from a global written test. A minimum score of 4/10 is required for each progressive test and the global written test, and the final grade must be 5 or higher to pass. Students can be exempted from the global written test if the weighted average of the two progressive tests is 6.5 or higher and no individual test score is below 5; in this case, the final grade is 90% from progressive tests and 10% from lab practices. If the average of continuous assessment tests is below 4, the final grade will be 100% from the global written test, provided all laboratory practices have been completed. For the extraordinary call, a single written exam (100% weight) is given, requiring a minimum score of 5/10 and completion of laboratory practices to pass.
